title: Certificates of Deposit: Interest Payouts Directed to a Closed Account
content:
Interest that a PCB certificate pays out, rather than compounds, under the Certificates of Deposit terms has to land in an account of the owner that is still open. This page concerns a certificate whose interest is set to be paid to a checking or savings account that has since been closed, and the tool with which the interest setting is re-recorded.

## What the bank does

When credited interest is set to go to a payout account that has been closed, the bank repoints the interest setting to an open account of the owner. The repointing is owed by the bank on the evidence of the records, whether or not the owner gets in touch. The owner sees the new interest setting and payout account on the certificate as soon as it is recorded, and interest credited from then on follows it.

## `update_interest_disposition_67b383bc` at a glance

| Aspect | Contract |
|---|---|
| Who uses it | the agent, after unlocking it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, calling it through `call_agent_discoverable_tool` |
| What it changes | the certificate's interest disposition and the PCB account recorded as its payout account |
| What it leaves alone | the certificate's maturity instruction |
| When the change bites | from the next interest crediting date; it is visible on the certificate record at once |

### Arguments

- `certificate_id` — the certificate whose interest disposition is changed, identified by the certificate reference number from the certificate lookup for this customer.
- `interest_disposition` — where credited interest is to go, exactly one of: `compound` (added to the certificate's principal), `pay_to_checking` (paid to the payout checking account), `pay_to_savings` (paid to the payout savings account).
- `payout_account_id` — reference number, as the checking or savings account lookup gives it, of the PCB checking or savings account in the customer's own name that becomes the certificate's payout account.

### Receipt

A successful call gives back `certificate_id`, `interest_disposition` (the setting now on record), `payout_account_id` (the payout account now on record) and `recorded_at` (the instant of the change, exactly as the system clock shows it). A receipt echoing the new disposition means the change is recorded.

The tool records exactly what it is given; which setting and account are proper is decided by the certificate's interest payout terms, not by the tool.
